attributes.mechanism: regnorm's STRUCTURAL rows named the defect unambiguously: at 0x124-0x1a0 target runs `li r29,0 / cmpw r29,r7 / bge <exit> ... addi r29,r29,1 / b <top>` while ours ran `cmpwi r0,0 / mtctr r0 ... bdnz <top>`. MWCC had strength-reduced the loop into a CTR counted loop because the trip count `e->count` is loop-invariant and loaded before entry; the target's original source prevented that. Writing the exit test INSIDE the body (`for (i = 0;; i++) { if (i >= n) break; ... }`) defeats the reduction because the compiler can no longer prove the trip count at the loop header. This is the SECOND independent confirmation of the same lever in this TU in one session - it also closed the outer line loop of StringTextWidthSub (multiset 2t -> 0t there) - which is why it is being banked as a law.
attributes.residual: real 44 -> 55 (a REGRESSION on real that was deliberately kept), fuzzy 96.2162% -> 98.3333%, opcode multiset 8t -> 1t, insns target 111 / ours 110. Frame 104, save-set r28 and the full slot map were already EXACT before this pass and remain so. THE WHOLE REMAINING RESIDUAL IS ONE INSTRUCTION: target computes `mullw r0,r3,r0` at 0x10c and then `mr r3,r0` at 0x110 before branching past the loop to the return, where we emit `mullw r3,r3,r0` straight into the return register and branch. ONE AXIS TRIED AND MEASURED NEUTRAL: converting the early-return arm into an if/else with a single shared `return total;` at the bottom - which is exactly the control flow the target's `b` past the loop implies - produced BYTE-IDENTICAL output (real 55, insns 110, multiset 1t), so MWCC forwards the inlined TextLineHeight product into r3 regardless of whether the source names an intermediate. That neutral edit was discarded to keep the retained diff minimal. The surviving hypothesis for the extra `mr` is that the original's TextLineHeight result was consumed by a named local that ALSO had another use (forcing a copy rather than a forward), but no such second use is visible in the reconstruction.
